svg.text: pale sand, a wet-sand band, a foam line; palms and dune grass behind
A. At fight distance, noon: the ground profile, the cover silhouettes, the far land as a value ladder. The two grey figures are 75 units tall (a fighter): scale only, no character art.
Palette at noon (the world-light tint per sky key multiplies it; lit, mid and shade are the three faces of one surface; the far ladder is each ridge hazed toward the horizon)

Readability (docs/art/dynamic-sky.md section 6): worst aura against any tone 20.6 CIEDE2000 (rule: 20 or more), worst Protagonist or rival body against ground, rock or vegetation 22.8 (rule: 15 or more), over every sky key with the world-light tint.
B. What the fight leaves: scorched (a beam along the ground), cratered (an impact), burned (fire on what grows)
a glassy black-green band fused into the sand (a beam path), its edge a
a shallow bowl in dry sand that floods from the water side: wet-sand dark
palms standing as black trunks with no crown, dune grass burnt to stubble,
grey ash drifted into the dune lee
C. Destruction in beach and coast: the impact at three moments (burst, peak, settle). Sand and spray: a wide pale plume that settles fast, and a ring of wet dark sand around the impact.
D. Where it meets its neighbours (hard steps in colour, never a fade; the cover mixes over about a third of the width)
Beach and coast to Open ocean
The sea shallows in three hard steps (deep, mid, shallow) and a pale foam line
runs along the sand; wet sand is a darker band above it.
Sand gives way to dune grass tufts, then grass; one low dune ridge between.
Dry scrub and driftwood on the sand; the sand stains toward red earth.
A palm line stands right on the sand, then the canopy wall; the jungle floor
begins at the back of the beach.
Tidal flats: sand turns to grey-green mud in steps, pools with a pale rim, reeds
The dune sea runs to the shore; only the sand colour steps from pale to gold; no
Beach and coast to Volcanic ground
Black sand beach: the sand steps from pale to grey to black, black boulders in
Coastal heath: the sand gives way to heather and bracken on a low cliff, grey
